summary: The record-g1 command works and its logic and tests are sound. Every listed check passes (87 gate tests, 1143 in make test, make check clean). The committed g1-record.json does not state the commit it ran on, although the story requires it. I rate that medium, which leaves the verdict FAIL. G1 is correctly recorded as PARTIAL because the T2-07 real-scene test is absent.

checks.evidence: ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy all clean

checks.criterion: AC1: gate test file and fixed test-id list (F1-F10 plus invalid-data tests of stories 1-3)
checks.evidence: fixtures/polarimetry/g1_required_tests.json (171 lines) lists the ids, and G1RequiredTests enforces exactly F1-F10 and T2-01..T2-03. The test file has 87 tests. I did not see the failing-first run, which is not reproducible from inspection.

checks.criterion: AC2: record-g1 CLI reads pytest junit, writes one GateRecord, never PASS for a missing, failed, skipped or xfailed required test
checks.evidence: polarimetry.py:2999-3250 (main, record_g1, _g1_status). GateRecord is built with gate_id G1, evidence_path, run_id None unless supplied, a scope string, and result as a JSON object of per-fixture counts. Skipped and xfailed tests count as skipped.

checks.criterion: AC3: status rules and the scope states whether the real-scene check was included
checks.evidence: _g1_status gives FAIL, NOT_RUN, PARTIAL or PASS. _real_scene_phrase writes 'not included (1 of 1 absent...)'. Tests at test_polarimetry_gate.py:435-483 cover absent, skipped and failed.

checks.criterion: AC4: output written to the given path, notes field records exact command and commit; only fixtures/polarimetry/g1-record.json written
checks.evidence: The command is recorded in result. GateRecord has no notes field, so nothing records the commit, and g1-record.json has no commit hash. Only fixtures/polarimetry/g1-record.json is written, and outputs/validation.json is untouched.

checks.criterion: AC5: failing-run test keeps the nonzero exit code; tampered report with a missing required test is not PASS; record validates against GateRecord; nulls stay null
checks.evidence: test_polarimetry_gate.py:890 (failing run, exit code), :917 (tampered report missing a test), :951 (tampered report with failures deleted), :562 (GateRecord validation, nulls stay null).

checks.criterion: Scope and safety: no files outside the story's list, no invented gate pass, config/run.yaml untouched
checks.evidence: The diff touches only fixtures/polarimetry/g1-record.json, fixtures/polarimetry/g1_required_tests.json, polarimetry.py and test_polarimetry_gate.py. The committed record is PARTIAL, not PASS.

findings.claim: The record does not state the commit it ran on, although AC4 requires the exact command and the commit.
findings.evidence: The T0 GateRecord has no notes field. The result JSON holds the command and the junit and required-list SHA-256 hashes, with no git commit or SHA. grep for 'commit' in the gate test finds only the committed-record path, so no test covers this.

resolution.reason: GateRecord (T0 schema, not owned here) has no notes field, so result now holds a notes object: the record-g1 command, the pytest command that wrote the report (--pytest-command, refused with exit 2 unless it names the given report with --junitxml or --junit-xml), the commit checked out at the repository root (git rev-parse, read-only) and uncommitted_changes (paths that differ from it in the index or work tree, plus untracked files git does not ignore). Outside a git checkout both are null, never guessed. Tests in 37e0bf2 use scratch git repositories built with plumbing. The committed record, regenerated in a4bb2b7, names commit 42e9f24 with only fixtures/polarimetry/g1-record.json uncommitted. A gate test requires the committed record's commit to be in the history and nothing but the record itself uncommitted.

findings.claim: The committed record's evidence_path is /tmp/terraluna-g1/junit.xml. That file is not in the repository, so the evidence cannot be re-checked from a clean checkout.
findings.evidence: The junit_sha256 is recorded, but the junit file is not committed under fixtures/polarimetry/. The story permits a path outside the repository.

resolution.reason: Story AC2 allows the junit path outside the repository. The report is pytest's own and carries hostname=platform.node(), the machine name (Codebase Patterns, story note 6), so committing it is a privacy choice the story notes leave to a human. It is not a defect. The record keeps the report's SHA-256, so any kept copy can be verified. Since 42e9f24 it also names the commit (42e9f24) and the exact pytest and record-g1 commands. From a clean checkout of that commit, the evidence can be re-created and its per-test outcomes compared with the record's counts. A new report has new timestamps and durations, so its hash differs and the outcomes are what to compare.

findings.claim: The CLI exits 1 for any non-PASS status, which matches the story's 'nonzero exit code is not hidden'. The G1 record stays PARTIAL until T2-07's real-scene test exists, which is intended.
findings.evidence: main() returns 0 only for PASS. g1-record.json status is PARTIAL with the oracle test listed as absent.

resolution.reason: This reports no defect. The finding itself says exit 1 for any status but PASS matches the story (AC5: a nonzero exit code is not hidden) and that PARTIAL until the T2-07 real-scene test exists is intended. Story note 1 fixes exit 0 only for PASS, 1 for any other recorded status and 2 when nothing is written, and test_deliberately_failing_run_records_fail_and_its_exit_code_is_not_hidden checks it on a real run. No change is needed.
